llm.summary: The skill's requests and runtime instructions are consistent with an email/verification-code automation tool: it only requires an API URL, an auth token, and a mailbox and makes HTTP calls to that service, with no install steps or unrelated secrets requested.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match what the SKILL.md instructs (receiving verification codes, sending/receiving email, extracting data). The declared required env vars (MAILS_API_URL, MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN, MAILS_MAILBOX) are appropriate for an HTTP-based mailbox service. Minor metadata inconsistencies: the registry summary lists no primary credential while the SKILL.md frontmatter sets primaryEnv: MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN, and SKILL.md version is 1.7.0 whereas registry metadata shows 1.7.1. These are bookkeeping issues, not functional mismatches.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are limited to making authenticated HTTP requests to the indicated API endpoints and using the declared env vars. They do not instruct reading system files or other environment variables. Note: the skill explicitly enables autonomous completion of sign-ups by waiting for verification codes (long-poll GET /api/code). That capability is coherent with the stated purpose but has an abuse surface (automated account creation) that operators should be aware of.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files, so nothing is written to disk or fetched during install. That is the lowest-risk install profile.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only three env vars are required (API URL, auth token, mailbox) which are proportional to the service. The SKILL.md uses exactly those vars. As noted above, the registry metadata's 'Primary credential: none' conflicts with the SKILL.md declaring MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN as primary; the token is legitimately sensitive and should be protected.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent system presence (always:false) and does not ask to modify other skills or system-wide settings. Model invocation is allowed by default (disable-model-invocation:false) which is expected for skills; that combined with its purpose increases potential impact if the token or API URL is malicious, but it is not a coherence mismatch.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims and only asks for an API URL, an auth token, and the mailbox address. Before installing: (1) verify the MAILS_API_URL is a trusted service endpoint you control or trust; treat MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN like any secret (store it securely, give it least privilege, rotate it if exposed); (2) be aware the skill is designed to automatically receive verification codes and can complete sign-ups — do not point it at a mailbox tied to sensitive accounts you don't want automated sign-ups created for; (3) confirm the publisher/owner if you require provenance (registry metadata has no homepage and the source is unknown); and (4) if you want to prevent autonomous actions, avoid granting the skill invocation privileges or restrict agent policies that allow automatic sign-ups. The minor metadata/version inconsistencies in the SKILL.md are bookkeeping issues but worth confirming with the publisher if provenance matters to you.
